item.name: OAuth 2.0
item.description:
Wahoo's authorization-code flow as its documentation describes it, read 2026-11-05. Fill client_id, redirect_uri and scope in an environment of your own and keep client_secret there, never in a shared collection.

The same facts, with each source sentence, at https://aifitnessapi.com/integrate/wahoo-api and https://aifitnessapi.com/tools/oauth-playground.

request.description:
https://api.wahooligan.com/oauth/authorize. Authorization URL (base_url is api.wahooligan.com). Open this URL in a browser (in Postman: copy it from the request bar); the user signs in and Wahoo redirects to {{redirect_uri}} with ?code=… Put that value in the auth_code variable.

Source: Wahoo Cloud API documentation, “Authentication”, https://cloud-api.wahooligan.com/

Scope: Space-separated, or set the app's scopes in the developer portal instead. Source: Wahoo Cloud API documentation, “Authentication”, https://cloud-api.wahooligan.com/

Documented scopes (joined with spaces):
- email: Access your email address
- user_read: Access your user data; without it the API returns 403
- user_write: Update your user data
- workouts_read: Access your workout history
- workouts_write: Update your workout history
- offline_data: Receive data even when the app is closed; needed for webhooks
- power_zones_read: Listed on Wahoo's developer portal, without a description
- power_zones_write: Listed on Wahoo's developer portal, without a description
- plans_read: Listed on Wahoo's developer portal, without a description
- plans_write: Listed on Wahoo's developer portal, without a description
- routes_read: Listed on Wahoo's developer portal, without a description
- routes_write: Listed on Wahoo's developer portal, without a description

PKCE: Supported once the app's Confidential field is set to No; S256 or plain. With PKCE the token and refresh calls send code_verifier instead of client_secret. Generate a verifier and challenge in your browser at https://aifitnessapi.com/tools/oauth-playground and put them in code_verifier and code_challenge. Source: Wahoo Cloud API documentation, “Authentication”, https://cloud-api.wahooligan.com/

https://api.wahooligan.com/oauth/token. Token URL. Wahoo documents the parameters in the query string of the POST.

Source: Wahoo Cloud API documentation, “Authentication”, https://cloud-api.wahooligan.com/

Wahoo documents the parameters in the query string of the POST.

Token lifetime: Two hours. Source: Wahoo Cloud API documentation, “Authentication”, https://cloud-api.wahooligan.com/

Note: From January 1, 2026, 10 unrevoked access tokens per user; unrevoked tokens are deleted 60 days after creation. Source: Wahoo Cloud API documentation, “Authentication”, https://cloud-api.wahooligan.com/

Note: Old tokens are revoked once an API call is made with the refreshed token. Source: Wahoo Cloud API documentation, “Authentication”, https://cloud-api.wahooligan.com/

Token lifetime: Two hours. Source: Wahoo Cloud API documentation, “Authentication”, https://cloud-api.wahooligan.com/

Note: From January 1, 2026, 10 unrevoked access tokens per user; unrevoked tokens are deleted 60 days after creation. Source: Wahoo Cloud API documentation, “Authentication”, https://cloud-api.wahooligan.com/

Refresh: Refresh returns a new access and refresh token. The previous pair is revoked only when an API call uses the new access token, so refresh just before a request: apps are limited to 10 unrevoked tokens per user.

Source: Wahoo Cloud API documentation, “Authentication”, https://cloud-api.wahooligan.com/

item.name: Webhook samples
item.description:
Wahoo's documented example notifications, sent to {{local_url}} (your local handler) unchanged. Signature: No signature. Wahoo sends the webhook_token you set in the app's webhook settings inside the JSON body; ignore any request without it. Source: Wahoo Cloud API documentation, “Webhooks”, https://cloud-api.wahooligan.com/

Headers that carry a signature hold the placeholder Wahoo prints, so a handler that verifies signatures will reject these: to send correctly signed requests, use https://aifitnessapi.com/webhooks/send-sample.mjs. Respond: An HTTP POST with Content-Type application/json; return HTTP 200. The users need the offline_data scope.

Payload library with JSON Schemas: https://aifitnessapi.com/webhooks#wahoo.

request.description:
Sent when a workout summary is available for a user whose token has the offline_data scope.

Wahoo's sample workout summary webhook message. Source: Wahoo Cloud API documentation, “Webhooks”, https://cloud-api.wahooligan.com/

Wahoo's example has the placeholder <webhook_token> where the token goes; the mock sender puts your token there and sends the rest unchanged.
